cells.tense: Right now you let what moves you become a direction to walk in.
cells.act: feed the drive a little at a time
cells.ask: Think of the path you're on. Give it one small bit of fuel this week — ten minutes, one call — before the pull fades, not after.
cells.core:
The feeling comes first, and the direction gets built out of it. Something stirs you, and instead of putting it away you turn it into a way to move — steady, goal-shaped, yours. That's the whole skill, and today it's working. You aren't forcing yourself forward. You're following a warmth that's genuinely there.

A direction like this runs on fuel. It stays alive because you feed it, a little at a time. So give it something small and regular, early, while you still feel like giving it. Staying fed is the practice, and keeping it warm is what the goal needs from you — not a push, not one big burst to make up for lost time.
cells.sheetLine: You're letting what you feel set the direction.
cells.verb: to sense what matters and move toward it
cells.place: where a life picks a direction and goes

cells.tense: You are reaching for a destination that isn't here yet, and pushing the pace.
cells.act: tend the small thing and learn from it
cells.ask: Choose something you're trying to grow — a habit, a project, a corner of your life. Work with it gently and watch how it takes hold. Learn its pace instead of setting one.
cells.core:
Direction has outrun feeling, and the goal gets pulled toward before it's ready. You want the outcome now, and that urgency takes you past the ground the whole thing stands on. The momentum was supposed to come out of what moves you. Today the motion has left the moving behind. It reads as drive, and it costs you the thing you're driving at.

So apprentice yourself to something small. Choose what you're trying to grow and work with it by hand, then watch how it actually unfolds. Nothing about the target — just the work and the watching. Your aim hasn't gone anywhere. It's simply not the task this week.
cells.sheetLine: The goal is ahead of you. Let the growing set the pace.

cells.tense: You are standing at a door that closed behind you, and haven't turned around.
cells.act: follow a raw curiosity with no use for it
cells.ask: Chase down a subject you're curious about — no use, no payoff, followed wherever it leads. No plan for it, nothing you'll get.
cells.core:
The sense of direction has gone quiet here, and the momentum went with it. Not because nothing stirs you — because what used to pull you forward is still back where you left it, and you haven't caught up to now. This is where a life picks a direction, and the picking is stalled. Nothing wrong is happening. The going has just emptied out where it used to run.

Don't try to force the momentum back. Get curious about some subject instead, and follow it with no goal in view. That kind of wondering returns first, and it brings direction along. Wanting to go somewhere starts with being interested in something.
cells.sheetLine: The door closed. You're still facing it. Turn around.

cells.tense: You are already steering toward something, and you don't count the steering as yours.
cells.act: put the inquiry on paper and follow it
cells.ask: Lay out what you've moved toward lately — a few lines, plain facts, in order, no feeling words. Then follow the question of whose hands did that.
cells.core:
You sense what matters and move toward it. That part is happening, and it's steady, and you don't describe yourself that way. By your account the direction is circumstance, or someone else's push, or simply what got done. Except the aim sits in your hands. It has sat there a long while. The steering keeps going without you claiming it in the version of events you tell.

So set out what you've been heading toward. Facts, in chronological order, no commentary. Seeing it in your own handwriting makes it a thing somebody did. The page asks for nothing else from you. It just shows the one who did it their own work.
cells.sheetLine: The wheel's been in your hands the whole time.
